live_candidates.description: The ESP32 CAM microcontroller, which powers this project’s complex door lock system, is seamlessly linked with cutting-edge face recognition software and Wi-Fi remote access. Apart from guaranteeing strong security protocols, the system has been expanded to encompass smooth interaction with home automation features, augmenting users’ total convenience and authority. The system’s key component, the ESP32 CAM microcontroller, makes use of its processing capability and integrated connection features. The system makes advantage of Wi-Fi connectivity to enable remote access, giving users the ability to monitor and control the door lock from any place with internet access. By allowing users to remotely give or revoke access, this feature greatly improves security and guarantees the integrity of the user’s property. A key component of the security architecture of the system is facial recognition technology. Based on facial traits, the system can precisely identify authorized users using a camera module interfaced with the ESP32 CAM. The use of this biometric authentication method strengthens security measures overall and provides an extra layer of protection by successfully blocking efforts by unauthorized individuals to gain access.

live_candidates.title: Embedded Facial Recognition-Based Smart Door Lock Using ESP32-CAM and Edge Impulse
live_candidates.description: The increasing demand for intelligent and contactless security systems has accelerated the development of biometric-based access control technologies. Conventional security methods such as physical keys and PIN-based authentication still suffer from several limitations, including key loss, password leakage, and unauthorized duplication. This research proposes a lightweight smart door lock system based on facial recognition using ESP32-CAM and Edge Impulse for embedded machine learning implementation. The proposed system performs real-time facial recognition locally on the ESP32-CAM without relying on cloud computing or continuous internet connectivity. The system integrates a solenoid door lock as the automatic access actuator and a buzzer as a warning indicator for unauthorized users. Facial image datasets consisting of registered and unregistered users were collected and trained using the Edge Impulse platform before deployment into the embedded device. System performance was evaluated under various testing scenarios, including distance variation, lighting intensity, face orientation, and partial face obstruction. Experimental results show that the proposed system operates reliably at distances between 15 cm and 35 cm and under lighting conditions ranging from 230 lux to 562 lux. The system also demonstrates stable recognition performance for frontal and moderate side-view face orientations. Performance evaluation using confusion matrix metrics achieved F1-scores of 90.9% and 88.9% for the two registered face classes, indicating reliable classification performance under practical indoor conditions. The experimental results confirm that the proposed ESP32-CAM-based smart door lock system provides a low-cost, lightweight, and effective embedded facial recognition solution for indoor smart security applications.

live_candidates.title: Intelligent Lock System with Facial Recognition and Fingerprint-Based Authentication Applications
live_candidates.description: In practical scenarios such as smart homes, offices, research laboratories, and restricted access facilities, there is a critical requirement for systems that provide secure, automated, and real-time access control. These environments demand reliable authentication mechanisms, continuous monitoring, and immediate alerts to prevent unauthorized entry. Traditional locking systems based on keys, PINs, or passwords are prone to theft, duplication, and hacking, while lacking real-time monitoring and remote accessibility. Furthermore, conventional systems do not integrate biometric verification or intelligent analytics, reducing their effectiveness in modern security applications. To address these challenges, the proposed Facial Lock Drive 2.0 utilizes the ESP32 microcontroller to develop a robust and intelligent access control system. The system integrates an ESP32-CAM for facial recognition and a fingerprint sensor for multi-factor biometric authentication, ensuring high security and accuracy. Upon successful verification, the ESP32 activates a DC motor to control the door locking mechanism, while an LCD display provides real-time system status and authentication feedback. Unauthorized access attempts trigger buzzer alerts, enhancing security awareness. IoT integration enables remote monitoring, access log management, and real-time notifications through cloud platforms. This smart system enhances security, eliminates the limitations of traditional locking methods, and provides a scalable, reliable, and intelligent solution for modern access control applications.

live_candidates.description: The ESP32-CAM Face Detection Automatic Door Lock System is a modern, AI-powered access control solution that enhances security through real-time facial recognition. This project integrates the compact and cost-effective ESP32- CAM module with a relay-controlled 12V solenoid lock, powered by a 12V battery regulated through a 7805voltage regulator to ensure stable 5V operation. The system provides a smart alternative to traditional lock-and-key mechanisms, aiming to reduce the risks of unauthorized access, lost keys, and forgotten passwords.The ESP32-CAM, equipped with a built-in camera and Wi-Fi capabilities, performs on-device face detection without requiring cloud connectivity, making it ideal for standalone and offline applications. live_candidates.title: Smart lock system with internet of things using facial recognition for home access
live_candidates.description: Security in urban residential environments is a significant challenge in regions with high crime rates and unauthorized access. This has led to the integration of internet of things (IoT) technologies and biometric authentication mechanisms into access control systems. Research has described smart lock solutions that require significant hardware resources or computationally complex recognition algorithms. This research proposes the implementation of a low-cost distributed architecture for facial recognition, lock control, monitoring, and supervision using mobile devices. The proposed architecture performs facial recognition using a histogram-oriented gradient (HOG) model executed on a desktop processing node, while an ESP32 microcontroller activates the lock. Remote monitoring is achieved through a communication framework using Flask libraries, tunneling with Ngrok, and a mobile application. Experimental validation was performed in a controlled environment, achieving 96.2% accuracy, and an F1-score of 95.9%. Furthermore, the control subsystem achieved an activation time of 0.78 seconds. The results validate the integration of biometric authentication, IoT control, and remote monitoring. However, limitations were identified in low-light or spoofing environments.

live_candidates.title: Design and Implementation of a Prototype Smart Door Lock Integrating Face Recognition and Smart Doorbell for Residential Access Control
live_candidates.description: Conventional residential door security systems generally rely on physical keys and often lack integrated user authentication and remote access management. This study presents the design and implementation of a prototype smart door lock that integrates face recognition, a smart doorbell, and remote access control for residential access management. The proposed system employs YOLOv8n for face detection, FaceNet for facial feature extraction, and cosine similarity for identity verification, while Blynk and Supabase support remote monitoring, visitor notifications, image storage, and mobile-based access control. Experimental results show that the face detection model achieved a detection rate of 100% at distances up to 300 cm. Face recognition achieved an accuracy of 92.44%, with 100% precision and specificity, while the prototype successfully authenticated registered users with a success rate of 91.11% and rejected all unregistered users. Furthermore, visitor notifications and remote door unlocking were completed with average response times of 2.60 s and 0.90 s, respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed prototype provides an effective and reliable solution for integrating face-based authentication, visitor management, and remote access control in residential environments.

live_candidates.title: A Smart IoT-Based Door Access Management System Using Facial Verification
live_candidates.description: Face recognition technology has emerged as an important advancement in modern security systems, offering a reliable and contactless method for user authentication. Earlier access control mechanisms primarily relied on physical keys, passwords, RFID cards, and biometric systems such as fingerprint scanners. Although these approaches improved security to some extent, they often suffered from limitations including key loss, password theft, card duplication, and physical contact requirements. As security threats continue to increase in residential, commercial, and institutional environments, there is a growing need for intelligent and automated access control solutions capable of providing higher levels of security, convenience, and real-time monitoring. To address these challenges, this study proposes an IoT-enabled face recognition–based door access control system that integrates facial authentication, automated door operation, cloud connectivity, and intrusion detection. The system utilizes a face recognition module to identify authorized individuals and communicates the authentication results to an ESP32 controller. Upon successful recognition, the controller operates a motorized door mechanism to grant access, while unauthorized attempts trigger a buzzer alarm and security notification. Through Wi-Fi communication, authentication events and intrusion alerts are transmitted to a cloud server for remote monitoring and record maintenance. The proposed framework enhances security by eliminating dependence on traditional keys and passwords while enabling contactless authentication and automated decision-making. Its ability to combine facial recognition, real-time alert generation, cloud-based event logging, and smart access management makes it a practical and scalable solution for modern smart homes, offices, laboratories, and other security-sensitive environments.
